S01.title: Headache and mild fever
S01.complaint: I have a headache and mild fever since yesterday.

answers.duration: Since yesterday evening — about a day now.
answers.symptoms: Mild fever, around 38 °C, and some body ache. No rash, no stiff neck, no vomiting, and I'm breathing fine.
answers.allergies: No, I'm not allergic to any medicine that I know of.
answers.meds: I'm not taking any medicines right now.
answers.history: No medical conditions. I'm generally healthy.
answers.lifestyle: I work in an office. Nothing unusual.

S01.seeDoctor: if the fever lasts more than 3 days, gets higher, or you develop a rash, stiff neck, confusion or difficulty breathing
S01.learning: A short-lived headache with mild fever and no red flags is commonly managed with a simple analgesic such as paracetamol or ibuprofen, after checking allergies and current medicines.

S02.title: Seasonal hay fever
S02.complaint: My nose keeps running, I'm sneezing all the time and my eyes are itchy. It happens every spring.

answers.duration: About a week. It's the same every year around this time.
answers.symptoms: Itchy watery eyes and a runny nose. No fever, no wheezing or chest tightness.
answers.lifestyle: I work from home, I don't drive much.

S02.seeDoctor: if you develop wheezing or breathlessness, or your symptoms don't improve within a week or two
S02.learning: Second-generation (low-sedating) antihistamines such as cetirizine, loratadine or fexofenadine are commonly used for hay fever. Wheeze or breathlessness needs referral.

S03.title: Heartburn after a heavy meal
S03.complaint: I've got a burning feeling in my chest after a big spicy dinner. I think it's acidity.

answers.duration: Started an hour after dinner. It happens occasionally after heavy meals.
answers.symptoms: Burning behind the breastbone that rises up. No pain in my arm or jaw, no sweating, no breathlessness, no trouble swallowing and no weight loss.
answers.history: No heart problems or other conditions.
answers.lifestyle: Office job. I sometimes eat late at night.

S03.seeDoctor: if it keeps coming back, lasts more than 2 weeks, or you have trouble swallowing, weight loss, vomiting or black stools — and call emergency services for chest pain spreading to the arm or jaw
S03.learning: Occasional heartburn after meals without alarm features can be managed with an antacid or alginate. Always rule out cardiac-type chest pain by asking about other symptoms.

S04.title: Small kitchen cut
S04.complaint: I cut my finger while chopping vegetables. It's only a small cut.

answers.symptoms: It's shallow and stopped bleeding after I pressed it. No numbness, I can move my finger normally.
answers.lifestyle: I had a tetanus booster two years ago.

S04.seeDoctor: if it becomes red, swollen, hot or starts oozing pus, if you develop a fever, or if it won't stop bleeding
S04.learning: Minor clean cuts: clean, apply antiseptic if desired, and cover with a plaster. Deep wounds, uncontrolled bleeding, numbness or signs of infection need medical care.

S05.title: Dry, cracked hands
S05.complaint: My hands are so dry and cracked from all the washing. Can you suggest something?

answers.duration: A few weeks — worse since winter started.
answers.symptoms: Just dryness and small cracks. No weeping, crusting or signs of infection.
answers.lifestyle: I wash my hands a lot at work in a kitchen.

S05.seeDoctor: if the skin becomes weepy, crusted or painful, or doesn't improve within 2 weeks
S05.learning: Emollients are the mainstay for dry skin — apply often and generously. Paraffin-based emollients carry a fire-risk warning.

S06.title: Mild diarrhoea
S06.complaint: I've had loose motions since this morning. What can I take?

answers.duration: Since this morning — about four times.
answers.symptoms: Mild cramps. No blood in the stool, no high fever, and I can keep fluids down.

S06.seeDoctor: if you notice blood in the stool, develop a high fever, show signs of dehydration (very little urine, dizziness), or it lasts more than 2 days
S06.learning: Fluid and electrolyte replacement (ORS) is the priority in acute diarrhoea. Loperamide may be used short-term by adults only when there is no blood or fever.

S07.title: Home thermometer
S07.complaint: I need a thermometer for home, for checking my kids' temperature.

answers.duration: Nobody is unwell right now — I just want one at home.

S07.seeDoctor: if a child has a high fever with a rash, breathing difficulty, drowsiness, or any baby under 3 months has a fever
S07.learning: Digital thermometers are accurate and easy to clean. A temperature of 38 °C or higher is commonly considered a fever.

S08.title: Painful mouth ulcer
S08.complaint: I have a painful ulcer inside my mouth. It hurts when I eat.

answers.symptoms: Just one small ulcer. No fever, no other sores, I'm otherwise well.
answers.history: I get one every few months, they heal in about a week.
answers.lifestyle: I bit my cheek by accident last week.

S08.seeDoctor: if the ulcer lasts more than 3 weeks, keeps coming back more often, or is unusually large or painless
S08.learning: Minor mouth ulcers usually heal within 1–2 weeks. Antiseptic mouthwashes or local anaesthetic gels can ease symptoms. Any ulcer lasting > 3 weeks must be referred.

S09.title: Mild sunburn
S09.complaint: I got a bit sunburnt at the beach yesterday. My shoulders are red and sore.

answers.symptoms: Red, warm skin on my shoulders. No blisters, no fever, chills or dizziness.
answers.lifestyle: I'm going outdoors again this weekend.

S09.seeDoctor: if you develop blisters over a large area, fever, chills, dizziness or confusion
S09.learning: Mild sunburn: cool the skin, moisturise with after-sun or calamine, drink fluids, and protect from further sun exposure. Extensive blistering or systemic symptoms need medical care.

S10.title: Dry tickly cough
S10.complaint: I've had a dry, tickly cough for three days. It's keeping me up at night.

answers.symptoms: Dry cough, a bit of a scratchy throat. No phlegm, no breathlessness, no chest pain, no blood.

S10.seeDoctor: if the cough lasts more than 3 weeks, you cough up blood, or develop breathlessness, chest pain or high fever
S10.learning: For a short dry cough, a cough suppressant or soothing linctus can help. Expectorants are meant for chesty coughs. Coughs > 3 weeks need referral.

S11.title: Chesty cough
S11.complaint: My chest feels heavy and I'm coughing up phlegm. Can you give me a cough syrup?

answers.symptoms: White phlegm. No fever, no blood, not breathless, no chest pain.
answers.history: No asthma, no heart or lung disease.

S11.seeDoctor: if the phlegm becomes green or bloody with fever, you become breathless or have chest pain, or the cough lasts more than 3 weeks
S11.learning: Chesty (productive) coughs are commonly managed with fluids and an expectorant such as guaifenesin. Cough suppressants are generally not used for productive coughs.

S12.title: Itchy, peeling feet
S12.complaint: The skin between my toes is itchy, white and peeling. I go to the gym a lot.

answers.symptoms: Itching and peeling between the toes. Nails look normal, no spreading redness, no fever.
answers.history: I'm not diabetic and have no circulation problems.

S12.seeDoctor: if it spreads, affects the nails, or doesn't improve after 2 weeks of treatment — people with diabetes should have foot problems checked
S12.learning: Athlete's foot is commonly treated with a topical antifungal (e.g., clotrimazole, terbinafine) plus keeping feet clean and dry. Diabetic foot problems need referral.

S13.title: Constipation
S13.complaint: I haven't been able to pass stools properly for four days. I feel bloated.

answers.symptoms: Bloating. No blood, no weight loss, no severe pain, no vomiting.
answers.meds: No medicines (no iron tablets or painkillers).
answers.lifestyle: I've been travelling and eating less fibre and water.

S13.seeDoctor: if you notice blood, unexplained weight loss, severe pain, or it lasts more than 2 weeks
S13.learning: Short-term constipation: increase fluids and fibre; bulk-forming or osmotic laxatives are common first choices. Red flags such as blood or weight loss require referral.

S14.title: Twisted ankle
S14.complaint: I twisted my ankle while jogging this morning. It's a bit swollen.

answers.symptoms: Mild swelling. I can walk on it, no deformity, no numbness.
answers.lifestyle: I run three times a week.

S14.seeDoctor: if you can't bear weight, there is severe swelling or deformity, or it isn't improving after a few days
S14.learning: Minor sprains: rest, ice (wrapped), compression and elevation, with topical NSAID or simple analgesia if suitable. Inability to bear weight needs assessment.

S15.title: Toddler nappy rash
S15.complaint: My 2-year-old son has a red nappy rash. What can I use?

answers.symptoms: Red skin in the nappy area. No blisters or pus, and he has no fever. He's eating and playing normally.

S15.seeDoctor: if the rash is severe, blistered, spreading beyond the nappy area, or the child develops a fever
S15.learning: Mild nappy rash: frequent changes, nappy-free time and a barrier cream such as zinc oxide. Severe or spreading rash, or fever, needs referral.

S16.title: Head lice
S16.complaint: The school called — my daughter has head lice. What should I use?

answers.symptoms: Itchy scalp and I can see live lice. No broken or infected skin.
answers.lifestyle: I'll check the rest of the family too.

S16.seeDoctor: if the scalp becomes infected or the treatment fails after two correct applications
S16.learning: Head lice products (e.g., dimeticone or permethrin lotion) must be applied exactly as directed and usually repeated after 7 days; check and treat affected family members only.

S17.title: Travel sickness
S17.complaint: I'm taking a long bus trip tomorrow and always get travel sick.

answers.duration: It always happens on long journeys.
answers.symptoms: Nausea during travel only. No other symptoms.
answers.lifestyle: I'm a passenger — I won't be driving.

S17.seeDoctor: if vomiting is persistent or you can't keep fluids down
S17.learning: Sedating antihistamines like dimenhydrinate can prevent travel sickness but cause drowsiness — check the person isn't driving and has no contraindications.

S18.title: Mild acne
S18.complaint: I keep getting pimples on my face. Is there something I can use?

answers.symptoms: Small spots and blackheads. No painful cysts or scarring.
answers.lifestyle: I wash my face once a day.

S18.seeDoctor: if acne is severe, painful, scarring, affecting your mood, or not improving after about 2 months of treatment
S18.learning: Mild acne is often managed with benzoyl peroxide, starting with a low strength. Severe, scarring or cystic acne needs a doctor.
